published_statement: RPP 2024, H MASS: '125.20 +- 0.11 OUR AVERAGE. Error includes scale factor of 1.4.' Inputs: 125.10 +- 0.11 (AAD 23BP ATLAS 13 TeV gg+4l), 125.46 +- 0.16 (SIRUNYAN 20L CMS 13 TeV gg+4l), 125.09 +- 0.21 +- 0.11 (AAD 15B LHC Run 1); ideogram chi2 = 3.7, CL = 0.159. RPP 2022, H0 MASS: '125.25 +- 0.17 OUR AVERAGE. Error includes scale factor of 1.5.' Inputs: 125.46 +- 0.16 (SIRUNYAN 20L), 124.86 +- 0.27 (AABOUD 18BM ATLAS 13 TeV gg+4l), 125.09 +- 0.21 +- 0.11 (AAD 15B); ideogram chi2 = 4.3, CL = 0.119.
published_hypotheses: Each average is a PDG weighted mean of mutually independent experiment-level combinations, with total errors, scaled by S = sqrt(chi2/(N-1)) because the inputs are mutually inconsistent (RPP 2024 p.3: S 1.4, CL 0.159; RPP 2022 p.2: S 1.5, CL 0.119).

The inputs are peak-position fits in gg and ZZ*->4l; results superseded by later combinations of the same experiment are listed under 'We do not use the following data for averages' (RPP 2024 p.1; RPP 2022 p.1) -- i.e. each edition's value is conditional on the measurements available at its cut-off.
No theorem is involved: both numbers are measurements with a stated 1-sigma error (0.11 GeV and 0.17 GeV).
hypothesis_drift: STATUS UNDER-CLAIMED (against the tree's own interest; recorded both ways) -- the pin 125.20 is labelled 'NAMED-NOT-READ; WITHDRAWN' (higgs.py:210; excite.py:382-385, 1063, 1170-1171; STATUS dict excite.py:389). It is READ here at source: the RPP 2024 average, 125.20 +- 0.11 GeV, S = 1.4 (pdg.lbl.gov 2024 listing p.1), also the 2025 edition (mass_width_2025.txt:48). The pin was a superseded edition, not a mistaken value. (Same finding as audits/pdg-2026-m_h.json; reproduced independently here.)

PROVENANCE UNNAMED -- the tree records 125.25 only as 'neither' of its own values (endpoint.py:581-582; endpoint.py:732 'a different PDG value, not an error'; excite.py:243-244, 1153). It is the RPP 2022 average 125.25 +- 0.17 GeV (READ, pdg.lbl.gov 2022 listing p.1), the same value in the 2021 and 2023 PDG tables. This adds to, and agrees with, the tree's reading; it does not contradict it.

DROPPED -- the uncertainties and scale factors. The tree carries both superseded values bare (higgs.py:210; endpoint.py:733, 959). 125.25 vs 125.20 differ by 0.05 GeV = 0.29 sigma of the 2022 error; W9(d)'s 'its figures were computed at m_h = 125.25' is therefore an arithmetic identification of the input, not a statistical discrimination -- and the tree states it as exactly that (endpoint.py:732 'not an error'). No conclusion depends on the dropped errors.

TREE-INTERNAL, NOT A SOURCE DRIFT -- the stated hypothesis '125.20 ... never used for a live figure' (excite.py:292-294; excite.py:1170-1171 'a record, never a live figure') fails at one site: excite.py:1210-1212, the D16 ULTRALOCALITY report table, prints cosine_response_error(LAMBDA_H_PIN_M / L) -- lambda_h at the withdrawn pin -- as 'exact error' beside address.ultralocality_error(L), which is computed at the READ m_h (address.py:688-689). The two columns are at different m_h; the pin column is -1.09e-3 (L = 1e-17 m) / -1.12e-3 (L = 1e-15 m) relative to its READ value. The selftest's matching check (excite.py:1510-1512) uses LAMBDA_H_READ_M, so it does not see the report line. A printed report figure, no verdict: a discrepancy, recorded, not repaired.

TREE-INTERNAL, STALE TEXT -- endpoint.py:578 'the spinodal e-fold ... is 4.486e17 times shorter' is the ratio at the withdrawn pin (4.4865e17); at the READ m_h it is 4.4839e17 (-> 4.484e17). endpoint.py:988-989 checks the live ratio against 4.486e17 at tolerance 1e-3, which exceeds the 5.6e-4 switch shift, so it passes. endpoint.py:756 labels the e-fold '(pinned m_h)' though spinodal_efold_s() now defaults to the READ M_HIGGS (endpoint.py:561). endpoint.py:582 says 'the tree pins 125.20' in the present tense after the switch. address.py:163 docstring gives 'lambda_h = ... = 1.5761e-18 m', which is lambda at 125.20 (READ gives 1.5770e-18). All presentation; no verdict uses them.

(C) lambda_h(125.20) = 1.576094e-18 m, e-fold(125.20) = 7.434922e-27 s, lambda_h(125.25) = 1.575465e-18 m (matches 1.5755e-18 at 2.2e-5; 125.20 misses at 3.8e-4); the three orchestrator figures jointly admit m_h in [125.2483, 125.2509] only. (E) excite.py:1211 prints a pin-based figure beside a READ-based one (rel. -1.09e-3); endpoint.py:578's '4.486e17' is the pin ratio (READ 4.484e17); address.py:163's '1.5761e-18' is lambda at the pin. lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested, evidence both ways. This entry is itself a record of earlier authors lacking data: RPP 2022's 125.25 lacked ATLAS's 2023 Run-2 combination (125.10 +- 0.11); with it RPP 2024 moved to 125.20. RPP 2024/2025's 125.20 lacked CMS's 2024 four-lepton Run-2 result (125.04 +- 0.12); with it RPP 2026 moved to 125.13. RPP 2026 itself lacks CMS's July 2026 diphoton Run-2 result (125.13 +- 0.15, arXiv:2607.28396), which retires the 2016 value 125.78 that dominates the average's chi2 (6.2 of 6.9); a sensitivity average with it is 125.086 +- 0.068 (S = 1.0). Every step moved toward the ATLAS/CMS cluster near 125.05-125.10 and every step was within 0.71 sigma of the prior edition's own stated error (0.29, 0.64 sigma; 0.96 sigma cumulatively from 125.25 to the sensitivity value). So the old values were not wrong: each was a correct average of the data then in hand, with an honest error that already covered the later value. Having the later data changes no conclusion the tree draws from these two numbers: W9(d) is an arithmetic identification of which value the orchestrator used (re-derived: only 125.25 fits its three figures jointly), and every figure the tree computes moves by <= 1.1e-3 under any of the moves, with no verdict attached to the digit. What the tree lacked is the reverse: it did not have (or did not read) the 2022 and 2024 listings, so it calls 125.20 NAMED-NOT-READ and leaves 125.25 unattributed, although both are READable PDG averages.
grade_evidence: Both superseded values are READ at source and are exactly what the tree says they are: 125.20 is the RPP 2024 (and 2025) PDG average, 125.20 +- 0.11 GeV (pdg.lbl.gov 2024 listing p.1), and 125.25 is the RPP 2022 (also 2021, 2023) average, 125.25 +- 0.17 GeV (2022 listing p.1); both averages were re-derived from their listed inputs, reproducing every printed PDG number (means, S, chi2, CL). The tree's figures at these values reproduce: lambda_h(125.20) = 1.576094e-18 m, e-fold(125.20) = 7.434922e-27 s, and the orchestrator's three figures (1.5755e-18 m, 2.4789e45 J/m^3, 4618) jointly admit only m_h in [125.2483, 125.2509] GeV -- 125.25, and no other PDG edition -- so W9(d) 'its figures were computed at m_h = 125.25' is confirmed, and the tree's own reading 'a different PDG value, not an error' (endpoint.py:732) is the correct one. The datum has moved twice (125.25 -> 125.20 -> 125.13) and a July 2026 CMS result would move it again (~125.09), but no conclusion moves: W9 falls on (a)-(c) independently and every figure shifts <= 1.1e-3. Recorded, not repaired, and not grade-changing because none touches the external result: the pin's status is under-claimed (NAMED-NOT-READ though READable); the tree's hypothesis 'never used for a live figure' (excite.py:292-294) fails at one report line, excite.py:1211, where the D16 table prints a pin-based 'exact error' beside a READ-based column; and stale pin-era text survives at endpoint.py:578 ('4.486e17', READ gives 4.484e17, passing endpoint.py:989 only through its 1e-3 tolerance), endpoint.py:756 ('(pinned m_h)'), endpoint.py:582 and address.py:163 ('1.5761e-18 m').
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a tree verdict (not a report line or docstring) shown to take 125.20 or 125.25 as a live input -- none found; the one live-looking use (excite.py:1211) prints a number and draws nothing from it. To WRONG: the orchestrator's figures failing to reproduce at 125.25 (they reproduce, and jointly exclude every other PDG edition), or the PDG 2022/2024 listings not carrying 125.25/125.20 (both READ). To DATA-DEPENDENT: some tree conclusion hinging on the difference between 125.25, 125.20 and 125.13 (all figure shifts <= 1.1e-3, no verdict at that digit). A future PDG average including arXiv:2607.28396 moves only the READ value (the pdg-2026-m_h entry), not this record.
